newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries drop as dlr slides, but fall limited.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries drop as dlr slides, but fall limited.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries edged lower across the board by Tokyo midday on Monday in reaction to the dollar's extensive slide against the yen in the morning, traders said.
But the fall in Treasuries was limited as no panic sales by Japanese investors were detected even after the dollar fell below the 118-yen level earlier, they said.
"Surprisingly, there have been no panic sales following the dollar's sharp fall," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
"Japanese investors are taking a wait-and-see stance. But given the strong underlying sentiment in the Treasury market, there should be ample bargain-hunting interest," he said.
The key 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 96-13/32, yielding 6.91 percent, compared with 96-20/32 in New York.
In addition to the dollar's movements, the market will be focusing closely on a series of U.S. inflation data scheduled this week before the FOMC meeting on May 20.
Traders said prices were lower both in the cash and futures markets, but there were no aggressive sellers as market thinness may have exaggerated the price fall.
The June T-bond futures contract was down 6/32 to 110-1/32 in late morning trade from the previous close, after falling as low as 109-28/32 earlier in the morning.
